prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck accident — the right lawyer depends on your case details, the lawyer’s trucking-specific experience, trial record, and how well you and the attorney work together. I can help you find strong candidates, but here’s a practical way to identify the best lawyer for your situation in Dallas.

What to look for
- Trucking-specific experience: experience with commercial truck cases, FMCSA regulations, logbooks, electronic control modules (ECMs), and cargo/maintenance issues.  
- Trial experience: many insurance companies only take big offers seriously when a lawyer will actually try the case.  
- Track record: significant settlements/verdicts in truck cases and references from former clients.  
- Use of experts: accident reconstruction, biomechanics, medical experts, and trucking industry specialists.  
- Resources: firm size and ability to front litigation costs for experts and discovery.  
- Communication & accessibility: who will actually handle the file (lead attorney vs. junior associate).  
- Fees & costs: contingency fee terms (common range ~33–40% before trial), and how costs are handled.  
- Credentials: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification (Personal Injury Trial Law), AV Preeminent or similar peer-review ratings, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers listings.

Important legal deadlines and facts
- Statute of limitations in Texas for most personal injury claims: 2 years from the date of the crash (exceptions apply). Don’t wait to get legal advice.  
- Trucking investigations require quick action (preserving ECM data, driver logs, video, and witness statements) — the earlier you hire counsel, the better.

Where to find and vet Dallas attorneys
- Texas State Bar Lawyer Referral Service and the State Bar website.  
- Directories: Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers (read peer and client reviews).  
- Look up jury verdicts and settlements (local court records) and firm press releases for case results.  
- Ask for client references and a clear explanation of how they handled a similar truck case.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many truck accident cases have you handled? How many year(s) of experience?  
- Have you tried truck cases at trial? How many verdicts/settlements?  
- What will you investigate immediately? Will you preserve the truck’s ECM and driver logs?  
- Which experts will you use? Who pays for experts?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? How will you communicate?  
- What is your contingency fee and how are expenses handled?  
- What outcomes do you think are realistic for my case?

If you’d like, I can:
- Compile a short list of well-regarded Dallas truck accident lawyers (based on directories and ratings) for you to call, or  
- Help draft an email or list of questions to use in consultations, or  
- Explain specifics if you give me details of the accident (injuries, date, location, insurer info).

Tell me which you prefer and any case details you’re comfortable sharing, and I’ll tailor recommendations.
